function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. It was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released in 1995. Here are some key points about Java:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Platform‑independent** | Java programs compile to bytecode that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The same bytecode can run on any device that has a JVM, making Java “write once, run anywhere.” |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything in Java is an object (except primitive types). It supports encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction. |
| **Strongly typed** | Variables must be declared with a type, and type checking occurs at compile time. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Java uses garbage collection to automatically reclaim memory from objects that are no longer reachable. |
| **Rich standard library** | The Java Standard Edition (SE) includes libraries for collections, networking, I/O, concurrency, GUI (Swing, AWT), and more. |
| **Multithreading** | Java has built‑in support for concurrent programming via threads and higher‑level concurrency utilities in `java.util.concurrent`. |
| **Security** | The JVM sandbox, bytecode verification, and security manager help protect against malicious code. |
| **Performance** | Just‑in‑time (JIT) compilation and runtime optimizations make Java programs fast enough for many high‑performance applications. |
| **Community & ecosystem** | Java has a vast ecosystem of frameworks (Spring, Hibernate), build tools (Maven, Gradle), IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse), and a large developer community. |

Java is widely used for building enterprise applications, Android mobile apps, web services, distributed systems, and even embedded devices. Its robustness, scalability, and portability have made it one of the most popular programming languages in the world.
